source.title: Error Bounds of Supervised Classification from Information-Theoretic Perspective
source.authors: Binchuan Qi; Wei Gong; Li Li

record.file_problem: Full text supplied. The empirical section uses and refers to figures whose plotted values are not numerically given in the text.
record.tranche_reason: The study uses its own measurements of fitting-error bounds, expected risk, and network depth on MNIST; these bear conceptually on V2 and on measured properties tracking the gap, but do not test the claim's random-label capacity or natural-label test accuracy directly.
record.gate_note: The paper reports theoretical bounds and MNIST experiments. Its comparisons of model risk and F(θ,qY|x) during training, and of depth versus the difference between risk and F, are results relevant to measured properties and model size. The paper gives no random-label experiments, no held-out accuracy comparison across widths beyond interpolation, and no architecture comparison of convolutional versus fully connected networks as described in V3.
record.test_reason: The study tests its own risk-bound quantities, not any listed version. Increasing depth and measuring risk minus F does not test whether widening beyond interpolation lowers test error (V2). F is not magnitude-aware sharpness, and its correlation with test loss does not test rankings of generalization gaps (V7). The theoretical discussion supplies no specific counterargument to either version.
record.authors_conclusion: The record broadly captures the authors' conclusion: they propose an expected-risk bound and claim positive correspondence with practical risk; their depth experiments show a smaller risk-minus-F discrepancy, which they interpret as reduced G and a tighter fitting-error bound. This interpretation is not a direct measurement of G. The empirical section compares F with conditional test loss rather than numerically evaluating the complete bound, and reports no correlation coefficient or statistical significance test.
record.recipe_differences: The experiments use MNIST, cross-entropy, batch size 64, momentum 0.9, learning rate 0.01 and one epoch; they study risk and bound quantities rather than the original claim's generalization comparisons.
record.method_sensitivity: The paper reports different convergence speed and expected risk for the residual-block architecture versus Model a, and reports plotted changes with depth k=1 to 4.

fits_no_version.finding: For both k=1 MNIST models, the authors report matching trends in conditional risk and F during training. Model b reportedly converges faster but reaches higher risk than Model a.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: The F quantity tracks conditional test loss during training in these two MNIST architectures.

fits_no_version.finding: For depths k=1 through 4, the authors report that greater depth reduces log(risk minus F) after training-loss convergence, interpreting this difference as an approximation to G.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Increasing depth reduces the reported risk-minus-F discrepancy in the tested MNIST models.

fits_no_version.finding: Proposition 6 conditionally bounds the loss Hessian's largest eigenvalue by the maximum structural-matrix eigenvalue; it does not measure magnitude-aware perturbation tolerance or rank generalization gaps.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Under the stated assumptions, structural-matrix eigenvalues bound Hessian curvature.

record.problems: The experiments use MNIST and one epoch, with no reported uncertainty or controls. The central comparisons are presented as plots without numerical values, and the paper describes them as applying to an arbitrary x.
record.rows_left_out: Figure 3 reports depth k=1 to 4 curves for both Model a and Model b, but exact values are figure-only and the text gives only an aggregate directional description. The rows cannot be assigned reliable condition-specific values or states; V2 therefore remains tested_not_extracted.

untested.parts: Random-label fitting and natural-label versus random-label held-out accuracy.
Width-dependent test error beyond the width needed for zero training error; no interpolation threshold is established.
Convolutional versus fully connected test performance and the contribution of local connectivity.
Adaptive optimizers versus SGD under limited or broader tuning.
Batch-size effects under fixed epoch budgets and adaptations that remove them.
Dropout effects, training-set-size dependence, and interactions with augmentation or weight decay.
Magnitude-scaled weight perturbations, their association with generalization gaps, and comparison with norm- and margin-based rankings.
Retraining after removal of highly memorized examples versus equally many random examples.

record.verdict_notes: Remove the record's tested_not_extracted designations for V2 and V7. Their exclusion follows from mismatched constructs, not merely unavailable figure values. The Figure 3 result is already declared in rows_left_out and bears on no listed version.

versions.untested_parts: No random-label training or natural-label held-out performance comparison.

Depth and parameter count are varied, but the text gives no numerical test-error values or explicit statement that widening beyond interpolation lowers test error; the relevant curves are figure-only.
No comparison of convolutional and fully connected networks on image test error.
The paper examines F(θ,qY|x) and expected risk during training, but does not measure magnitude-aware sharpness or compare it with norm- or margin-based measures.
No removal of memorized training examples.
